paragraphs.title: A Call to Praise from the Heavens

answers: The angels and all his hosts
The kings of the earth only
easy.explanation: The verses call the angels and all the heavenly hosts to praise the LORD.
easy.q: Who are called to praise the LORD in these verses?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Praise ye him, sun and moon” and “all ye stars of light.”
easy.q: Which heavenly bodies are mentioned in these verses?

easy.explanation: The fourth verse mentions “the waters that be above the heavens.”
easy.q: What else, besides the heavens, is called to praise the LORD?

answers: Because he commanded, and they were created
medium.explanation: The psalm says, “For he commanded, and they were created.”
medium.q: Why does the heavenly realm praise the LORD?

medium.explanation: A “decree” is an established command or order made by the LORD.
medium.q: In verse 6, what does the word “decree” most nearly mean?

answers: From the heavens to nature and animals
From the higher realm to the heavenly bodies and upper waters
medium.explanation: The verses move from angels and heavenly hosts to the sun, moon, stars, heavens, and waters above the heavens.
medium.q: What is the general order of the call to praise in verses 1–6?

answers: God’s creation and established order provide the basis for its praise
Its praise comes from ruling over the earth
The verses make no connection between creation and praise
challenge.explanation: The verses explain that God commanded them, created them, and established them forever.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the creation of the heavenly realm and its praise?

challenge.explanation: Verse 6 says, “He hath also stablished them for ever and ever.”
challenge.q: Which word emphasizes that the heavenly realm continues to exist for a long time?

answers: The call to praise includes different parts of the heavenly creation
The verses concern only the stars
challenge.explanation: The verses include angels, heavenly hosts, the sun, moon, stars, heavens, and upper waters.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the call to both angels and heavenly bodies?

paragraphs.title: A Call to Praise from the Earth

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “Praise the LORD from the earth.”
easy.q: From where are the creatures of the earth called to praise the LORD?

answers: Fire, hail, snow, vapour, and stormy wind
easy.explanation: The eighth verse lists fire, hail, snow, vapour, and stormy wind.
easy.q: Which natural phenomena are mentioned in these verses?

answers: Beasts, cattle, creeping things, and flying fowl
easy.explanation: Verse 10 mentions beasts, cattle, creeping things, and flying fowl.

answers: Sea creatures and abysses, natural forces, plants, and animals
medium.explanation: The verses move from the dragons and deeps to weather, mountains, trees, and animals.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the parts of creation called to praise?

medium.explanation: “Vapour” refers to mist, steam, or moisture in the air and is listed among the natural phenomena.
medium.q: In verse 8, what does “vapour” most nearly mean?

answers: Because they include waters, weather, plants, and animals
Because they concern only human beings
medium.explanation: The verses mention the deeps, weather, mountains, hills, trees, beasts, creeping things, and birds.
medium.q: Why can these verses be said to include the whole natural world?

answers: The call to praise includes both natural phenomena and living creatures
Only animals are part of creation
Natural forces are shown as opposing the LORD
challenge.explanation: The verses call both the forces of nature and many kinds of living creatures to praise.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from including natural forces alongside animals?

answers: Mountains, hills, fruitful trees, and cedars
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 specifically mentions “fruitful trees, and all cedars.”
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the verses include plants and not only animals?

answers: It limits the call to one type of creature
It shows that the call encompasses the natural world in its many forms
It explains only the origin of the wind
challenge.explanation: The list includes waters, weather, landscapes, plants, animals, creeping things, and birds, emphasizing the breadth of the call.
challenge.q: How does the detailed list contribute to understanding the call to praise?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 mentions the kings of the earth, princes, and judges.
easy.q: Which people with positions of authority are called to praise the LORD?

answers: Young men, maidens, old men, and children
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children.”
easy.q: Which age and gender groups are mentioned?

answers: The children of Israel and his saints
easy.explanation: Verse 14 speaks of “his saints” and “the children of Israel, a people near unto him.”
easy.q: To whom is the LORD’s nearness especially emphasized at the end?

answers: From important people to people of every age
medium.explanation: The verses first mention kings, nations, princes, and judges, then people of various ages and genders.
medium.q: How does the call to praise expand in verses 11–12?

medium.explanation: The word “excellent” describes the greatness and superiority of the LORD’s name.
medium.q: In verse 13, what does “excellent” most nearly mean?

answers: Only human beings praise the LORD
The LORD’s name alone is exalted, and praise encompasses earth and heaven
medium.explanation: The psalm says that his name alone is excellent and that his glory is above the earth and heaven.
medium.q: What is the central conclusion of these verses?

answers: The call includes all people, while the ending especially emphasizes the LORD’s nearness to Israel and his saints
The call is only for Israel and excludes other nations
The ending cancels the call to all people
challenge.explanation: The verses address kings, nations, rulers, judges, and people of every age, then highlight the LORD’s nearness to his people.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the universal call to praise and the emphasis on Israel at the end?

answers: Maidens and children are also included
challenge.explanation: Verse 12 explicitly includes young men, maidens, old men, and children.
challenge.q: Which detail might be overlooked but expands the group of those called to praise?

answers: Praise is limited to human beings
The conclusion connects human beings with all creation in earth and heaven
The heavens are excluded from the conclusion
challenge.explanation: The phrase broadens the conclusion beyond humanity to the whole realm of earth and heaven.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “his glory is above the earth and heaven” after the description of human beings?
